title: Transpose of the strict normalized Hom numerator for arbitrary coefficient modules
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a site small in the module universe, $R$ a sheaf of commutative rings, $P$ a flat-term K-flat complex of $R$-module sheaves, $C$ any unbounded $R$-complex, and $T$ any $R$-module sheaf, regarded as a complex in degree zero [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] [def-pc-kflat-complex]. Use localization $Q$, the normalized derived tensor-Hom structure $H_R$, and its fixed Hom representative and inverse localized augmentation [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] [def-coef-ringed-tensor-hom-model] [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] [def-coef-hom-representative-evaluation]. In the strict models [def-sfb-internal-hom-strict-models] [def-sfb-internal-hom-strict-roof], write $\eta_M:M\to I_R(M)$, $J=I_R(C)$, $B=\mathcal Hom_R^\bullet(P,J)$ and $A=T\otimes_R B$, where $\otimes$ is the actual total sheaf tensor. Let $a_T:A\to\mathcal Hom_R^\bullet(P,I_R(T\otimes_R J))$ be the fixed normalized comparison. Then evaluation into $QC$, under $QB\cong H_R(QP,QC)$, is represented by $\operatorname{ev}_J:B\otimes_R P\to J$, $f\otimes p\mapsto f(p)$, followed by $[\eta_C]^{-1}$. There is a chain map $h_T:A\otimes_R P\to T\otimes_R J$ with formula $(t\otimes f)\otimes p\mapsto t\otimes f(p)$ on every slice and homogeneous total-tensor summand. The uncurried chain map of $a_T$ is exactly $\eta_{T\otimes_R J}\circ h_T$, tested with the actual product-Hom projections and sheafification units. Consequently the derived tensor-Hom transpose of $[a_T]:QA\to H_R(QP,Q(T\otimes_R J))$ is $[h_T]$. Here $Q(A\otimes_R P)$ computes $QA\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}QP$; neither $A$ nor $T$ is required to be flat. These identifications are natural in $T$, contravariantly in $P$, and covariantly in $C$, and commute with compatible coefficient maps and inversion of quasi-isomorphisms of the complex representatives. The tensor order is $A,P$, so no interchange sign is inserted. No boundedness, finite generation or continuity assumption is made.

proof.text: Put $N=T\otimes_R J$ and $E=I_R(N)$. The fixed augmentation gives K-injective $J$ and $E$, and isomorphisms $[\eta_C]$ and $[\eta_N]$. Apply [lem-sfb-hom-kflat-chain-transpose] to the arbitrary complex $B$ and $1_B:B\to\mathcal Hom_R^\bullet(P,J)$. Its transpose is $[\operatorname{ev}_J]$, with $\operatorname{ev}_J(f\otimes p)=f(p)$. The fixed representative factorization and inverse augmentation of [def-coef-hom-representative-evaluation] identify evaluation into $QC$ with $[\eta_C]^{-1}[\operatorname{ev}_J]$. This uses the K-injective representative $J$ of $QC$, not a new resolution of it.

For $f$ of degree $n$ and $p\in P^m$, the balanced assignment $((t,f),p)\mapsto t\otimes f^m(p)$ respects restrictions on every slice. The universal properties of the two sheaf tensor products extend it uniquely to $(T\otimes B^n)\otimes P^m\to T\otimes J^{n+m}$; the total direct-sum inclusions define $h_T$. To check the chain condition, the image of the source differential on this summand is
$$t\otimes(d_B f)(p)+(-1)^n t\otimes f(d_Pp)=t\otimes d_Jf(p),$$
because $(d_Bf)(p)=d_Jf(p)-(-1)^nf(d_Pp)$. This is the target differential, since $T$ has degree zero. The summand coproduct and sheafification universal properties extend the equality to all sections; no assertion that all sheaf-tensor sections are global pure tensors is used. There is no permutation of $f,p$.

The normalized comparison is the fixed one in [def-sfb-internal-hom-strict-roof]. Its normalization in [def-sfb-internal-hom-strict-models] says, after the actual $(m,m+n)$ product-Hom projection and evaluation on the identity of each slice,
$$a_T(t\otimes f)(p)=\eta_N(t\otimes f(p)).$$
Thus the chain uncurrying of $a_T$ and $\eta_N\circ h_T$ agree after each total summand inclusion and each sheafification unit, by step 2. First the tensor-product universal property, then the sheafification adjunction, and finally the total coproduct universal property make these maps equal. Product projections specify the actual value of $a_T$; no alternate Hom model is substituted.

Apply [lem-sfb-hom-kflat-chain-transpose] to $A$, $E=I_R(N)$ and $f=a_T$. The hypotheses are precisely the given flat-term K-flatness of $P$, the K-injectivity from step 1 and no restriction on $A$. It identifies $Q(A\otimes_R P)$ with $QA\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}QP$ and represents the transpose into $QE$ by $[\eta_N\circ h_T]$ using step 3. For the fixed representative of $H_R(QP,QN)$, [def-coef-hom-representative-evaluation] prescribes the inverse localized augmentation on the output. Hence the requested transpose is
$$[\eta_N]^{-1}[\eta_N\circ h_T]=[h_T].$$
In particular we have never asserted that tensoring with the possibly non-flat $T$ preserves arbitrary quasi-isomorphisms.

For $u:T\to T'$, the two routes in the evaluation square send $((t\otimes f)\otimes p)$ to $u(t)\otimes f(p)$. For $v:P'\to P$, precomposition gives $h_{T,P'}((t\otimes(f\circ v))\otimes p')=t\otimes f(vp')=h_{T,P}((t\otimes f)\otimes vp')$. For $w:C\to C'$, postcomposition gives $(1_T\otimes I_R(w))h_{T,C}((t\otimes f)\otimes p)=t\otimes I_R(w)(f(p))=h_{T,C'}((t\otimes(I_R(w)\circ f))\otimes p)$. The tensor and sheafification universal properties used in step 2 give these as chain-map equalities. The augmentation equation $I_R(z)\eta=\eta z$ makes the corresponding squares for $a_T$ commute by step 3. The natural comparisons and transposition in [lem-sfb-hom-kflat-chain-transpose], with the fixed natural augmentation, therefore give the asserted derived squares.

For a quasi-isomorphism in $C$, two-out-of-three for the natural augmentations makes $I_R(w)$ a quasi-isomorphism between K-injectives. For a quasi-isomorphism between the allowed $P$ representatives, [lem-pur-rhom-well-defined] applies with the identity on $J$. The resulting maps of $B$ are quasi-isomorphisms between K-injectives, since [lem-pur-hom-kflat-into-kinjective] applies to each $P,J$. By [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] all these maps, and $I_R(w)$ itself, are homotopy equivalences. Tensoring with $T[0]$ preserves them: a homotopy $s$ is sent to $1_T\otimes s$, and $d(1_T\otimes s)+(1_T\otimes s)d=1_T\otimes(ds+sd)$. Thus the induced changes of $A,N$ are invertible after localization even for non-flat $T$. Step 5's commutative squares remain commutative on inverting these isomorphisms (multiply the square equation by the two inverses). The representative tensor comparisons also commute with inversion by [lem-sfb-hom-kflat-chain-transpose].

proof.text: Finally a compatible coefficient map means the given maps on the coefficient modules and Hom representatives respect evaluation and the fixed augmentation comparisons. On every slice, if the induced semilinear maps are denoted by $\alpha_T,\alpha_P,\alpha_J,\alpha_B$, compatibility says $\alpha_B(f)(\alpha_P(p))=\alpha_J(f(p))$. The two paths for $h$ are therefore both $\alpha_T(t)\otimes\alpha_J(f(p))$. This proves the coefficient square on the actual generators and hence on sheafified total tensors by step 2. The compatible augmentation square gives the same equality for $a$, by step 3; applying its inverse after localization gives the same square for the transpose, by step 4. Identity maps and successive coefficient maps obey the same equation by substitution. This is compatibility with supplied evaluation-preserving coefficient comparisons, and makes no claim that arbitrary extension of scalars commutes with infinite Hom products. All calculations apply in every integer degree; none requires boundedness, finite generation or continuity.
